newsitem.title: UK: Dry cargo freight market shows signs of recovery.
newsitem.headline: Dry cargo freight market shows signs of recovery.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) recorded its first gain since August 23, rising 2 points to 994 amidst a number of positive aspects on Thursday's dry cargo freight market.
Brokers suggested that with the good fixture turnover in the Far East and better volume of enquiry in the Atlantic the Panamax market had at last bottomed out.
In addition demand for smaller handy-sizes on the Continent and from the Lakes has risen sharply, even if the larger craned bulkers remain out of favour in almost all areas.
There is little to suggest any significant improvement yet in Caper prospects.

Grain -- Cargill have dominated the latest Atlantic grain transactions. Kleon 105,000 dwt was fixed on private terms up River and Brazil to the Continent in a quiet South American market, and an unnamed Panamax was covered for 60,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Continent for Oct 5/10 at an unchanged $8.00.
It was not clear if Cargill fixed Barcelona-Hamburg range option UK for this business but they were again in the market on this basis for repeat business.

Cargill were also reported to have covered up to 55,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for Oct 18/25 at $19.00 basis no combo, the same rate as Dreyfus fixed for this position last Tuesday but 25 cents up on Halla's overnight fixture of Top Trader.
Pressure for Lakers continued and Brodin fixed the 20-year old Alpha 28,193 dwt delivery spot Gibraltar for a Lakes rod at a firm $7,500 daily.
There was also strong pressure for small handies for grain from the Continent which one broker described as a "pretty fruity market".
Glencore, for example, quoted at least 3 barley orders - 20/25,000 Rouen/Cuba, 25,000 Cardiff/Red Sea, and also Antwerp and Spanish Med to China, all for early shipment.

Groupe Pantin fixed a 19,000 dwt vessel from North France to West Africa at an economical $5,850 daily. South African grain rates by comparison were especially weak with Andreooking Tassos for 30,000 maize Durban/Puerto Cabello for Ely Oct at $15.50.
Minerals in the caper category Nessie was believed fixed for 100,000 ironore Nouadhibou/Taranto at about $3.00 and Hassbat Qatar 120,000 Narvik/Antwerp by Cobelfret on private terms.
Coe and Clerici were linked with Amstelwal 134,638 dwt for Hampton Roads coal to Brazil.
But the main action was with Panamaxes in the East where brokers said a number of vessels fixed at higher rates on private terms.
Among these may be the Safmarine-Relet Sapphire 68,600 dwt, Torm Tekla 69,268 dwt for Richards Bay/Continent and Darya Preeth 73,200 dwt, all understood to be fixed on subjects.

Armada are said to have paid about $7,750 daily for Joyous Age 69,271 dwt delivery Taiwan for 3-5 months, and Hai Kang 70,000 dwt was reported fixed delivery W C India by Goldbeam at $7,800 for a similar period.

Wadi Al Arab 63,800 dwt was booked by Elkem delivery Japan trip via Australia to the Continent at under $4,000 daily in the Atlantic Elcano fixed a Panamax bauxite stem Kamsar/Comfort at $4.35, down 15 cents from last done.

Handy-sizes for Laker sizes and smaller bulkers the Continent is a strong market, but less so for the larger geared tonnage. World Agamemnon 37,000 dwt fixed about 30 days Mediterranean steel business at close to 5,500 daily.
S Africa is especially weak - Velebit 42,000 dwt is understood to have gone as cheaply as a similar vessel Elli for a trip to the Far East at $8,00daily plus about $100,000 bonus.
